description: Byte-exact golden reference outputs for the Go codefang + uast tools, for validating the Rust rewrite. Captures with machine=true AND nonBinding=false are BINDING: the Rust port must reproduce them byte-for-byte. nonBinding=true captures are either human formats (cosmetic) or machine formats that are intrinsically nondeterministic in the Go tool (Go map-iteration order in per-file/per-pair sections) and must be compared after canonicalization.

binaries.buildVia: make build (CGO_ENABLED=1, static libgit2 from third_party/libgit2/install)
binaries.codefangVersionNote: the `version` subcommand embeds the build timestamp via -ldflags and is NOT deterministic; it is not a report and is not captured.

envNote: Set exactly these vars AND use `set -f` (noglob) before each command so a literal '*'/'static/*' analyzer selector reaches the binary. Only STDOUT is captured; STDERR (timestamped progress logs) is discarded. Cross-run state is disabled via --checkpoint=false --resume=false --no-cache and wiping ~/.codefang/checkpoints.

inputs.staticSubsetNote: STATIC analyzers are nondeterministic and produce huge output on the full repo; they are captured on this fixed 10-file subdirectory (passed via -p) bounded by --head, single-worker. This is the canonical static golden ('fast deterministic subset'). HISTORY analyzers run on the full repo bounded by --head/--limit.
inputs.streamNote: ndjson and timeseries+ndjson are STREAMING formats: one JSON line per commit, emitted during the streaming pipeline and EMPTY in --head mode. They are captured with --limit N --workers 1 (no --head), which is deterministic for a fixed HEAD.
inputs.uastFileNote: uast parse/analyze/query operate on this file's working-tree bytes and embed its ABSOLUTE path in the output; the Rust harness must invoke with the identical path.

formats.runFormats: codefang run --format: json yaml plot bin timeseries ndjson text compact (default json). timeseries+ndjson = `--format timeseries --ndjson`.
formats.uastParseFormats: uast parse --format: json compact tree none (default json). yaml NOT supported.
formats.uastAnalyzeFormats: uast analyze --format: text json html (default text). yaml NOT supported.
formats.uastQueryFormats: uast query --format: json compact count (default json). yaml/text NOT supported.
formats.compactNote: run --format compact is a human progress-bar format (empty for combined '*' selections and for history analyzers); treated as nonBinding.
formats.binNote: bin is binary; outPath holds raw bytes and sha256 is the stable comparison hash. bin is STABLE for history analyzers but UNSTABLE for static analyzers (map ordering).
formats.plotHtmlNote: run --format plot/html render multi-page HTML to a DIRECTORY (-o), not stdout; their stdout golden would be empty. Not captured (nonBinding by nature).

nondeterminismNote: The Go tool emits per-file (static) and per-pair (couples/shotness) sections in Go map-iteration order, which is randomized per process. Sorted content is identical across runs; only byte order differs. Such captures are recorded with stable=false, nonBinding=true. The Rust harness must canonicalize (sort those arrays by file_path / key) before comparing, OR the Rust port may emit them in a deterministic (sorted) order, which is a correctness improvement over Go.
stabilityNote: Every machine capture ran twice with identical env/argv (set -f). stable=true means both runs produced an identical sha256; only those are BINDING.

captures.note: static/clones, format json, subset (--head, single worker)
captures.triageVerdict: GO-NONDETERMINISTIC AT CONTENT LEVEL (not sortable). Clone-pair representative is tie-broken by Go map-iteration order: across two Go runs the emitted pair name flips (e.g. 'Int64.Has <-> String.HasAny' vs 'Int64.Has <-> Int64.HasAny'), byte length varies. No Rust sort can reproduce it. Stays nonBinding.

triageNote: Step 16 triage (2026-06-06): each machine&&stable=false capture was run twice via the Go ref AND twice via the Rust release binary. RESULT: Go is nondeterministic across its OWN two runs for ALL 22 (the golden sha never reproduces), so category (a) 'Rust-missing-sort -> byte-identical' has ZERO members. Two sub-causes: PURE-REORDER (deep-sorted content equal: cohesion/comments/complexity/composition/imports/couples/file-history) where the Rust port should emit a deterministic SORTED order as a correctness improvement (still not byte-identical to the unstable golden), and CONTENT-NONDETERMINISM (clones/halstead/shotness, and all_static which unions them) where the actual data differs run-to-run and no sort helps. All 22 correctly remain stable=false/nonBinding. See per-capture triageVerdict.
